beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — the spindle assembly checkpoint gate logic
beats.narration_text: The spindle assembly checkpoint is M-phase's all-clear gate. Every chromosome pair must be attached to spindle fibers from both poles before anaphase can proceed. One unattached kinetochore is enough to hold the whole thing.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — two states labeled BLOCKED and RELEASED; unattached kinetochore with wait signal; anaphase arrow blocked by orange bar

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — checkpoint failure → aneuploidy → cancer
beats.narration_text: When this checkpoint fails, sisters separate before all chromosomes are pulled correctly — some cells get too many chromosomes, some too few. That aneuploidy is a hallmark of cancer. This plate shows exactly why one unattached pair is enough to stop the clock.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the spindle-checkpoint plate from plates underscore gen dot py p-zero-seven into Manim. Two states — top and bottom, stacked vertically. Top state: dashed metaphase plate, GREEN pole dots at each end, four chromosome pairs as BLUE circle pairs, pair index two unattached — it gets a short free line and a VERM starburst wait signal, the other three get spindle lines to both poles. Block the anaphase arrow with an ORANGE bar. Bottom state: all four pairs connected, no starburst, bar lifted, arrow clears to a cluster of separated sisters. Animate top state then bottom state.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_SpindleCheckpoint class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The two-state structure is one helper function called with different arguments — build underscore state takes a y-offset and two booleans: all underscore attached and gate underscore open. That one function renders both the blocked and the released configuration. The chromosome pairs are a list comprehension of four VGroups, each containing two circles offset by eighteen Manim units left and right. The unattached pair at index two skips the spindle lines to both poles and instead gets a short free line plus a starburst from Flash geometry. The ORANGE bar is a Rectangle placed at the arrowhead position.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_SpindleCheckpoint
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
config.background_color = "#FFFFFF"
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; ORANGE="#E69F00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_SpindleCheckpoint(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    # Top state: blocked
    top = self.build_state(y_off=1.6, all_att=False, open=False)
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(m) for m in top],
      lag_ratio=0.14, run_time=1.8))
    self.wait(0.4)
    # Separator
    sep = DashedLine([-6.5,0,0],[6.5,0,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.2)
    self.play(Create(sep), run_time=0.3)
    # Bottom state: released
    bot = self.build_state(y_off=-1.8, all_att=True, open=True)
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(m) for m in bot],
      lag_ratio=0.14, run_time=1.8))
    self.wait(0.6)

  def build_state(self, y_off, all_att, open):
    mobs=[]
    plate=DashedLine([-4,y_off,0],[2.4,y_off,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=2.2)
    mobs.append(plate)
    for px,py in [(-4.8,y_off),(2.8,y_off)]:
      mobs.append(Dot([px,py,0],radius=0.12,color=GREEN,
        fill_opacity=0.9))
    xs=[-2.9,-1.4,0.1,1.6]
    for i,x in enumerate(xs):
      for dx in [-0.22,0.22]:
        mobs.append(Circle(0.2,color=BLUE,fill_color=BLUE,
          fill_opacity=0.28,stroke_width=2.2).move_to([x+dx,y_off,0]))
      if all_att or i!=2:
        mobs.append(Line([x,y_off,0],[-4.8,y_off,0],
          color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.5))
        mobs.append(Line([x,y_off,0],[2.8,y_off,0],
          color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.5))
      else:
        mobs.append(Line([x,y_off,0],[x-0.5,y_off-0.3,0],
          color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.5))
        mobs.append(self.starburst([x-0.7,y_off-0.5,0]))
    if open:
      mobs.append(Arrow([3.2,y_off,0],[5.0,y_off,0],
        color=GRAY,stroke_width=3))
      for dx,dy in [(-0.3,-0.3),(0,-0.3),(0.3,-0.3),
                    (-0.3,0.3),(0,0.3),(0.3,0.3)]:
        mobs.append(Circle(0.18,color=BLUE,fill_color=BLUE,
          fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([5.2+dx,y_off+dy,0]))
    else:
      mobs.append(Arrow([3.2,y_off,0],[3.9,y_off,0],
        color=GRAY,stroke_width=3))
      mobs.append(Rectangle(0.3,0.9,fill_color=ORANGE,
        fill_opacity=0.65,stroke_width=3,
        stroke_color=ORANGE).move_to([4.0,y_off,0]))
    return mobs
props.sparkLine: One gap, one starburst, full stop.

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_SpindleCheckpoint — two states, top blocked, bottom released
beats.narration_text: Run it. Top state: the dashed metaphase plate draws, pole dots appear, chromosome pairs fade in left to right — three pairs get full spindle connections, pair three gets a short free line and the starburst. The ORANGE bar appears at the arrowhead. Then the separator draws and the bottom state builds: all four pairs connected, no starburst, the arrow clears past where the bar was, and the separated sister clusters appear at the right.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: animate the TRANSITION between states instead of building two static states. Build the top blocked state. Then animate the release: the starburst fades out, spindle lines grow to connect the unattached pair to both poles, the ORANGE bar moves upward and fades out, the arrow grows past where the bar was, and the chromosome pairs separate and migrate toward the poles.

claude "Revise: animate the TRANSITION between states instead of building two

beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_SpindleCheckpointRelease — blocked → transition → released
beats.narration_text: Watch the transition now. The blocked state builds — starburst fires on the unattached pair, bar sits at the arrow. Then the starburst fades. Spindle lines grow to both poles for the previously unattached pair — watch them extend to each GREEN dot. The bar shifts up and fades out. The arrow grows past where it was. Then the chromosome pairs separate: each blue pair drifts toward its pole. That migration is anaphase — one clear signal removed, and the whole division resumes.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: One unattached pair, one signal, the whole division halted. The transition animation showed how removal of that one signal releases the gate — and what happens if it releases prematurely.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — summary card: SAC = single-pair sensitivity; premature release = aneuploidy; 'strip this pattern for any binary gate'

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a zoom-in beat on the unattached kinetochore — show the MCC, the mitotic checkpoint complex, as a small cluster of three labelled dots on the kinetochore face: Mad2, BubR1, and Bub3. Why run it? Because the starburst is evocative but abstract. The MCC is the actual molecular machinery that broadcasts the wait signal. Zooming in and labelling the three proteins makes the checkpoint mechanistic, not just schematic — and it teaches the student exactly which proteins a spindle checkpoint drug needs to target.
